entries.title: Cover 1 baseline
entries.summary: A single deep safety structure with man coverage underneath is a common Cover 1 baseline; actual rules and leverage vary by system.

entries.title: Cover 2 baseline
entries.summary: A two-deep structure can divide deep responsibility between two safeties with underneath defenders handling shorter zones; variants can alter those rules.

entries.title: Cover 3 baseline and match variants
entries.summary: A Cover 3 baseline divides the deep field into three zones, but match variants such as Rip/Liz can convert responsibilities based on receiver releases, so SAGE must distinguish spot-drop labels from pattern-match rules.

entries.title: Cover 4 / quarters baseline
entries.summary: Four-deep/quarters structures distribute deep responsibility across corners and safeties; match-quarter systems add formation and route-dependent rules that cannot be captured by a static four-zone diagram.

entries.title: Simulated pressure
entries.summary: A defense can threaten pressure with multiple potential rushers yet rush only four, changing which defenders rush/drop while preserving a conventional rush count. SAGE must not equate a pressure presentation with a blitz.
fantasyImplications: Potential effects on protection identification, QB processing and route timing require empirical validation.

entries.title: Coverage-rule granularity may outperform simple man/zone splits
entries.summary: Player/offense matchup models may improve when match rules, shell rotation and pressure presentation are distinguished from coarse man/zone labels.
